entries.english:
Disputes between Rosenberg or Hatzfeldt and Hohenlohe.

Term: 1535, 1665–1570, 1589–1652.

Contents: 1. mediation by Bishop Friedrich of Würzburg in disputes between Count Ludwig Kasimir von Hohenlohe-Neuenstein and Zaisolph von Rosenberg over tithes in the Wieset and Münster districts; Count Ludwig Kasimir’s incursion into Rinderfeld and Streichental and removal of 40 wagonloads of grain, 1561; 2. legal dispute between Count Wolfgang von Hohenlohe-Weikersheim, plaintiff, and Georg Siegmund von Rosenberg over the seizure of two Hohenlohe acorn-mast pigs in Weidensee, 1589–1594; 3. litigation before the Imperial Chamber Court between Rosenberg and Hohenlohe over hunting in Lindach and Aichholz and in Reckersfeld Forest, 1535, 1556–1567, 1592–1597; 4. disputes over hunting in Lichte Eichen and Lehenhölzlein in the Streichental district, 1590; 5. disputes between Hohenlohe-Waldenburg and Finsterlohe on one side and Rosenberg on the other over sheep driving at Vorbachzimmern, and disputes between Rosenberg or Hatzfeldt and Hohenlohe over the so-called Streit tithe at Pfitzingen, 1556, 1567, 1590, 1600–1652; 6. miscellaneous disputes between Hohenlohe-Waldenburg and Rosenberg after the settlement concluded in 1569, (1569) 1570; 7. seizure of two horses belonging to Rosenberg subjects at the Hohenlohe toll at Riedbach, 1564.

Extent: 1 volume, folios 1–270.
